name: Theodore Roosevelt
role: 26th president of the United States (1901-1909); Progressive (Bull Moose) Party candidate (1912)
summary: A Republican-turned-Progressive who as president and in his 1910-1912 New Nationalism backed strong federal regulation of corporations, labor protections, graduated income and inheritance taxes, conservation, and direct democracy such as primaries, recall and the popular review of some state court decisions. He was also a firm advocate of naval and military strength, American expansion and tutelage over peoples he judged less advanced, and the Americanization of immigrants, and held race views that were hierarchical but reportedly changed late in life.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Platform proposed a single national health service for public health and social insurance against sickness, but not state-funded care for everyone.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Platform pledged minimum wage standards for working women to provide a living wage; said no one is a good citizen on less than a wage above bare cost of living. Not stated as a general or large increase.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Held that the public welfare outranks market outcomes and that government must supervise business and set rates (railroads), while not opposing business as such.

public-ownership.rationale: Platform said natural resources should be owned or controlled by the nation and urged government acquisition of railroads in Alaska; no call to own major industries generally.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Urged a graduated income tax and an inheritance tax so that large fortunes bear a rising share of taxation.

unions-good.rationale: Wrote that he became a strong believer in labor unions and the rights of labor; said corporation and labor union alike have come to stay and are each a source of good if properly managed. Also condemned union lawlessness.

property-fundamental.rationale: Said every man holds his property subject to the community's right to regulate its use as the public welfare requires, and that he put human welfare ahead of property when they conflict.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Demanded strong national regulation of interstate corporations by a federal commission; said corporate wealth must be under publicity, supervision and regulation, while accepting large corporations.

cut-welfare.rationale: Platform pledged social insurance against sickness, unemployment and old age and industrial accident compensation; also said he would not carry a man who lies down.

strong-leader.rationale: Held that the executive may do whatever the Constitution and Congress do not forbid, and the New Nationalism was impatient of deadlock from divided powers; also opposed one-man rule and limited his own terms.

state-harmful.rationale: Held that government must act actively and affirmatively for the people; New Nationalism asked for greatly broadened federal power.

empower-police-military.rationale: Called for a strong navy and a trained reserve and said every young man owes preparation for service.

decide-locally.rationale: New Nationalism put national need before sectional advantage and platform sought national jurisdiction over problems beyond individual states.

traditional-family.rationale: Said the success of civilization depends on citizens being sound in their home and the father and mother of healthy children, and warned of race suicide.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Held the crucible must turn out Americans of one American nationality, not dwellers in a polyglot boarding house.

gradual-change.rationale: Warned that excess is followed by reaction, but pressed for large reforms including recall of state court rulings.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Sought strict exclusion of undesirables and ratio limits on vessels but said we cannot have too much immigration of the right sort.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: In 1910 proposed a League of Peace of great powers to enforce peace by force if necessary, while saying no international police yet exists.

free-trade.rationale: Platform denounced the Democratic tariff-for-revenue-only policy as leading to widespread industrial and commercial disaster and backed a protective tariff.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Wrote that outside powers have a sheer duty to interfere in massacres like those of the Armenians and defended the intervention in Cuba.

limit-growth.rationale: Platform said conservation must not retard legitimate development; resources should be generously used.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Called the inheritance tax a far better tax than income tax and urged a graduated inheritance tax on large estates.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Platform: believe in a protective tariff that equalizes competition and warned that tariff for revenue only would cause industrial disaster; also wanted downward revision and a tariff commission.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Inferred: his stated republican principles (government by the people through elected representatives) do not accommodate hereditary rule.

democracy-best.rationale: Defended popular rule, saying people are masters of their Constitution, but also warned about the quality of citizenship.

direct-votes.rationale: Platform urged initiative and referendum on the states and wanted more direct action by the people under proper safeguards.

right-to-secede.rationale: Praised the Union cause and said the men who fought in 1861 were right.

war-builds-character.rationale: Said the nation that has lost the fighting edge is in a dangerous and ignoble position and praised war's manly virtues.

military-superiority.rationale: Said the navy must be maintained and increased in efficiency and kept strong relative to other nations'.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Wanted a single American nationality formed by assimilating German, Irish and other immigrants, though his racial writings favored Anglo-Saxon expansion.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Rejected Marxian theory as refuted and condemned class hatred as a basis of politics.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Wrote that Indians never had real title to the land and the continent could not be kept as a game preserve for squalid savages (though later as president defended Indian land rights against fraud).

self-interest-moral.rationale: Condemned sordid materialism and pursuit of mere wealth as a measure of worth.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Treated suffrage and citizenship as duties first; said no law avails without character and the duty of public service.

limit-population.rationale: Warned against race suicide and said a people's failure to bear children is the greatest failure.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Wrote that he supports any businessman, labor leader or reformer, including socialist proposals, when he believes their methods serve the people, and opposes them otherwise.

direct-action.rationale: Condemned mob violence and lawlessness by workers as firmly as corporate greed and sought change through law and elections.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Held that civilization's advance over savagery was ultimately righteous and necessary.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Called orthodox Marxian economic socialism an exploded theory and said profits of legitimate business are justified by public benefit.

taxation-theft.rationale: Argued for higher and graduated taxes as a legitimate government power over fortunes and bequests.

harm-principle.rationale: Said there should be complete liberty for each man to live as he desires provided he does not wrong his neighbor, while supporting wide regulation of business and labor.

conscription.rationale: In 1917 emphasized the need for universal military service and held it a duty of young men to be ready for war.

positive-liberty.rationale: Said no man can be a good citizen on a bare-subsistence wage and long hours, and that conditions keep countless men from fulfilling citizenship.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Held neo-Lamarckian race views and wrote that blacks were as a race inferior; but by 1917-18 reportedly rejected racist hereditarian theory. Evidence mixed.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Defended the historic American policy of expansion and national responsibilities in Hawaii, Cuba, Puerto Rico and the Philippines.

class-collaboration.rationale: Insisted on justice to both employers and workers, condemned class hatred, and framed reform as fair dealing between the two sides.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Favored women's suffrage as an equal right, yet platform backed special protections for women's work and he stressed motherhood as woman's primary duty.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Platform wanted Alaskan coal opened to development at once under government ownership and public coal and oil lands used under lease.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Said immigrants must Americanize in speech, ideas and loyalty, that there is room for one language only, and that hyphenated Americans have no place.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Platform said both old parties had become tools of corrupt interests and described an invisible government linking corrupt business and politics.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Wrote in 1914 that criminals should be sterilized and feeble-minded persons forbidden to leave offspring.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Advocated an active state: labor regulation, social insurance, trust supervision, conservation, and the executive as steward of public welfare.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Said each man should be treated on his merits and defended a square deal, but also wrote of racial hierarchy and dismissed aboriginal claims; views reportedly shifted late in life.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Praised righteous war and called a war with savages the most ultimately righteous of wars; backed intervention and expansion.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Preached the strenuous life of struggle and held that nations that avoid strife decline; described conquest by strong young races as the engine of history.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Platform sought to prohibit injunctions in labor disputes that would not issue otherwise, and in 1907 said some criticism of labor injunctions is warranted.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: In WWI called pacifists who supported Germany traitors and demanded unreserved national loyalty.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Said limited terms check dictatorship and declined a third term in 1908, though he ran for a non-consecutive third term in 1912.

recall-officials.rationale: Platform urged recall of officials, and he asked that unfaithful public servants be removed easily and surely.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Wrote of savagery versus civilization and the dominant world races, and held that advanced societies must lead others.

minority-language-support.rationale: Said there is room for but one language in this country, English.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: In Santo Domingo, ran the custom-houses so creditors were paid and revolution-driven debts settled; backed enforcement rather than cancellation.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Platform wanted currency control lodged with the government and protected from Wall Street, and opposed a privately controlled system.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Said property rights are subordinate to the community's right to regulate its use to whatever degree the public welfare requires.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Said it was right to reject the counsels of peace in 1861 for the Union.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Urged a graduated income tax of the proper type and graduated inheritance taxes.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Opposed hyphenated loyalties and insisted all immigrants become Americans and nothing else.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Called materialistic Marxian socialism an exploded theory and stressed character and moral awakening as essential to progress.

ban-cartels.rationale: Said blanket prohibition of combination is futile, but urged strengthening the Sherman Law against agreements to divide territory or limit output and directed suits against trusts.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Platform demanded restricting courts' power so the people hold ultimate authority on social-welfare law via a vote on state judicial decisions; kept federal Supreme Court review.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Said the US must train Filipinos for self-government and administered Cuba, Santo Domingo and Panama; called leaving the islands infamy.

public-money-creation.rationale: Platform said issuing currency is fundamentally a government function, called issue through private agencies harmful, and opposed the Aldrich plan for leaving currency in private hands.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Argued that correcting evils through reform answers socialists and populists, and rejected Marx's predictions as falsified.

elective-rulers.rationale: Inferred: his platform calls for government of the people through elected representatives and direct primaries; he did not address inheritance of rule.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Told the privileged that much has been given and much should be expected, and rejected the multimillionaire of mere wealth as an asset.

notes: Positions are drawn from his presidency, the 1912 campaign and his autobiography; the 1912 platform is a party text he led. Secondary sources (Wikipedia, citing Dyer and Dalton) are used for Brownsville, Americanization quotes, the 1914 sterilization statement and the view that his racial views shifted by 1917-18; the Osawatomie speech was read as an excerpt only. Race views are marked contested (low) because they changed over time. Dyer and Dalton were not opened directly.
